note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

item-quality.verdict: The item is basically sound but should be revised before acceptance. It is solvable from the instruction plus the start graph, and the instruction does not leak the solution: it never mentions strobes, PMT or the cmd port. Every number the oracle uses is stated, and the start graph fails only on f2p (3000 Hz / 0.5). No valid alternative was wrongly rejected. Five alternatives passed: strobe wired straight to cmd with the random strobe removed, both message paths, single-quoted float keys, the dict held in a variable, and a renamed File Sink with a ./ relative path (all in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-06/itemq/). A negative-frequency answer was correctly rejected. The surviving problems are about how precise the oracle is and how the item is labelled. (1) Medium: the 'keep the timing of the switch' requirement accepts a switch anywhere from about 0.43 s to about 1.28 s (reference 0.683 s). The seed's original 1000 ms period passes 6/6, and its original strobe timing passes 5 of 7 runs, so the timing perturbations are not enforced and scoring is non-deterministic in the 1.1-1.3 s band. (2) Medium: L1 is wrong under proposal §5.2, which lists message ports as L3; the inventory's L1 estimate comes from the seeds.py 'msg' hint not matching 'message'. (3) Low: tone purity is unchecked, so square-wave or DC-offset outputs pass. (4) Low: the modify vs parameter-tune label is borderline because the reference is a single parameter-value edit. Probe scripts are in C:\Users\Lenovo\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Lenovo-Documents--MScAC-2701-ml-ops-project-project\e3a3c780-e6be-4b4a-8abe-931944b53353\scratchpad\rev06\ (probe.py, switch.py, bf.py). The task directory was not modified.

findings.claim: The stated requirement 'keep the timing of the switch' (about half a second) is only loosely checked. The oracle accepts a switch landing anywhere from about 0.43 s to about 1.28 s into the captured stream, while the reference switches at 0.683 s. Two of the nine perturbations (Message Strobe period 1000->500 ms and random-delay 200/40->100/20 ms) are therefore not protected: the seed's original timing passes most of the time, and in the 1.1-1.3 s band the same answer passes or fails at random.
findings.evidence: Measured the first sample with |x|>1.0 over 6 runs each (scratchpad rev06/switch.py). Reference: 0.683 s in 6/6. Period 1000 ms (the unperturbed seed value): 1.109-1.28 s, passes V6 in 6/6. Original seed timing (period 1000, mean 200, std 40): 1.195-1.28 s, passes in 5 of 7 runs; the 7th, a './gb ladder' run, failed f2p rms at 1.12. Period 1100: passes 4/6. Period 250: switch at 0.427 s, passes 4/6. Period 900: passes. Random-delay mean 500 ms: passes. Only 1200 ms and above, and 200 ms and below, are reliably killed. The mutation gate tried only extreme timing breaks (period 3000, random strobe sending the retune at about 0.1 s, throttle bypass), so it stayed at 100 %. Cause: the pre window is 0-0.4 s and the post window is 1.25-1.75 s, and the switch time is quantised to 4096-item steps (0.085 s). Graphs: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-06/itemq/mut_period_*.grc and mut_orig_timing.grc.
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten the windows around the measured switch time: pre window 0-0.5 s (skip 0, n 24000) and post window 0.95-1.45 s (skip 45600, n 24000). The switch cannot land before 0.5 s because the strobe sleeps 500 ms before it first fires. Add mutants for period 1000 (the original seed) and period 250. Re-run the gates at 8-way concurrency to confirm the reference still passes 10/10. Also reconcile the instruction's 'about half a second' with the 0.68-0.77 s actually visible in the file, for example 'roughly half a second after the start (it shows up about 0.7 s into the file)', so a tightened window is not a hidden requirement.

findings.claim: Level L1 is wrong under the proposal's definitions. The whole task is about message ports: a PMT dict travels from Message Strobe to Message Strobe Random-Delay to the Signal Source's cmd port. Proposal §5.2 lists message ports as an L3 trait, and the graph is not a single-rate streaming chain because it has an asynchronous message side-graph. The seed inventory's 'L1' estimate comes from a heuristic bug.
findings.evidence: Proposal line 83 defines L3 as '(> 15 blocks, multi-rate, tags/PDUs/message ports, OFDM, Embedded Python)'. src/grcbench/tier_f/seeds.py:40 has L3_HINTS = (..., "msg", ...), which is meant to send message-port graphs to L3. But the block ids are blocks_message_strobe and blocks_message_strobe_random, and neither contains the substring 'msg', so features() falls through to L1 (reports/seed_inventory.md: 'analog/sig_source_msg_ports.grc | L1 | 5'). The approved plan (Phase 3) also says L1 tasks come 'from the deterministic composer of ≤ 5-block single-rate chains', L2 from converted examples, and L3 is deferred to W5. Labelling this L1 would pull down per-level L1 pass rates with a message-port task.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel the item L3, or record it as an explicit deviation approved by the team. Add 'message' (and e.g. 'strobe') to L3_HINTS in seeds.py, then re-derive the level estimates in reports/seed_inventory.md so other message-port seeds are not mislabelled the same way.

findings.claim: The instruction describes the output as a tone, but the oracle checks only peak frequency and RMS. Outputs that are no longer a pure tone pass V6.
findings.evidence: Changing the Signal Source waveform to analog.GR_SQR_WAVE passes V6 (pre rms 0.787, post rms 1.2, peak 1500/4200 Hz), although only 42 % / 41 % of the power lies within ±50 Hz of the tone and the post-switch mean is 0.6+0.6j. Sending {"freq": 4200, "ampl": 1.2, "offset": 0.3} also passes (post rms 1.237, within 5 %). For comparison, the reference band fraction is 0.9994 before the switch and 1.0000 after it (scratchpad rev06/bf.py; graphs itemq/mut_square_wave.grc, itemq/mut_offset_0p3.grc).
findings.suggested_fix: Add band_fraction checks: at least 0.99 of the power in 1450-1550 Hz in the pre window (group p2p) and at least 0.99 in 4150-4250 Hz in the post window (group f2p). Each check maps to 'the output is a single tone'. Add a waveform mutant and an offset mutant to the mutation list.

findings.claim: The family is borderline: the item is labelled modify, but by the brief's own definition it is closer to parameter-tune. The reference differs from start.grc in exactly one parameter value (the Message Strobe's msg). The instruction states only a target behaviour and leaves the model to find which parameter controls it, which matches the brief's parameter-tune definition: 'state the target behaviour; the model decides which parameters to change'.
findings.evidence: Diffing start.grc against reference.grc shows a single line change: msg 'pmt.to_pmt({"freq": 3000, "ampl": 0.5})' -> 'pmt.to_pmt({"freq": 4200, "ampl": 1.2})'. The repo convention is inconsistent: the fixture fx_modify_tone and gbf-dev-03 label single-parameter edits 'modify', while gbf-test-11 and gbf-test-12 label similar retunes 'parameter-tune'.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the team settle the modify vs parameter-tune boundary across the first set (for example, modify = a structural or behavioural change the user names; tune = reach a numeric target by changing values only) and relabel this item to match. If it stays modify, add a note explaining why.

compliance.verdict: Mostly survives: gbf-test-06 is correct, solvable, unambiguous on its main edit and compliant on every required field. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates and all gates passed. gates.json came out byte-identical (sha256 593bb0a3…): solvability 10/10, 451/3000 tokens, 3/3 variants pass, the start fails at V6 (f2p fails, p2p passes), 12/12 mutants are valid and the kill rate is 1.0. The other checks also held. The seed analog/sig_source_msg_ports.grc is in the test split and its sha256 2c3fe219… matches the installed example. license, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, id/dir/split and the observation contract all follow the rules. The canary is only in task.json. Disjointness from reports/reference/training_task_specs.json holds: no training spec uses message strobes or cmd ports. Running build.py from a scratch copy regenerated task.json, start.grc, reference.grc and all 3 variants byte-identically. The start state behaves as the instruction says (1500 Hz / 0.8, then 3000 Hz / 0.5, switch at 0.68 s). The reference passed 24/24 runs at 12-way concurrency and 16/16 at 8-way under a 16-core CPU hog, with zero spread in the measured values. One finding refutes part of the item: the 'timing of the switch' property is not really checked. Wrong answers that double the switch time, including going back to the original seed's 1000 ms period, pass V6. Two near-edge timing changes pass or fail at random. Everything else is low severity: wording, documentation, licence notices and harness notes. I did not edit the task; gates.json was rewritten with identical bytes. Scratch work is in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-06.

findings.claim: The spec property 'the switch still happens about half a second after the start (not at the start, not much later)' and the instruction's 'keep ... the timing of the switch' are not enforced. The oracle accepts a switch anywhere between about 0.4 s and 1.25 s of captured stream, so wrong answers that halve or double the timing pass. For two of them the verdict is random (7/8).
findings.evidence: No oracle check has requires = the timing property; the only enforcement is the gap between the windows (p2p 0-0.4 s, f2p 1.25-1.75 s). Probes on the reference, 8 runs each at 8-way: Message Strobe period 1000 ms (switch at 1.11 s, about twice the reference's 0.60-0.77 s; 1000 ms is also the un-perturbed seed value) passed V6 8/8. Message Strobe Random-Delay mean 400 ms (switch at 0.85 s) passed 8/8. Period 1100 ms passed 7/8 and period 250 ms (switch at 0.43 s) passed 7/8, so the same wrong answer passes or fails at random. The timing mutants in task.json are all gross (period 3000, early random strobe, throttle bypass), which is why the mutation gate does not catch this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an f2p check on a short window just after the nominal switch, for example skip 0.95 s, n 0.15 s: peak_freq 4200 ±1 % and rms 1.2 ±5 %. Keep the p2p pre-window ending at about 0.4-0.45 s. Add mutants for period 1000 ms, period 250 ms and random-delay mean 400 ms. Then repeat the 8- to 12-way and CPU-load reruns. I observed switches between 0.597 s and 0.768 s; by construction the strobe cannot fire before 0.5 s.

findings.claim: 'Keep everything else as it is:' is followed by a list that leaves out the random phase resets. An answer that removes the Message Strobe Random-Delay passes V6, even though it breaks the literal 'everything else'.
findings.evidence: Probe: delete blocks_message_strobe_random_0 and connect blocks_message_strobe_0:strobe straight to analog_sig_source_x_0:cmd. All checks pass: 1500 Hz / 0.8 p2p, 4200 Hz / 1.2 f2p, switch at 0.597 s. task.json notes say the phase resets are deliberately not checked, but the instruction does not tell the model that.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the sentence so the list is the whole requirement, for example 'Keep the 48 kHz sample rate, the initial 1.5 kHz tone with amplitude 0.8, the timing of the switch and the complex output ... unchanged', and drop 'everything else'. The other option is to add a pre-switch check that the phase resets are still there.

findings.claim: build.py and task.json notes overstate the timing margin. They say the switch appears at 0.68-0.77 s with at least 0.28 s of margin, but it also lands at 0.597 s (7 x 4096 items).
findings.evidence: build.py docstring: 'the retune appears in the captured stream at 0.68-0.77 s ... with >= 0.28 s of margin on either side'. task.json notes: 'measured switch in the captured stream at 0.68-0.77 s'. My reruns of the reference measured 0.5973 s in 2/24 runs at 12-way, and also in the strobe-direct and freq-4250 probe runs. The real margin to the 0.4 s end of the pre-window is about 0.2 s. This does not cause flakiness: the reference passed 40/40 runs, including under a CPU hog, and the strobe cannot fire before 0.5 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the notes and the docstring to 'switch at 0.60-0.77 s; margin >= 0.19 s before / 0.48 s after'.

findings.claim: None of the released .grc files keep the GPL seed's copyright holder or author, and neither does task.json. The perturbation record does not list this removal or the change of the flowgraph id.
findings.evidence: /usr/share/gnuradio/examples/analog/sig_source_msg_ports.grc has options author 'Marcus Müller', copyright '2020 Free Software Foundation' and id 'demonstrate_signal_source_message_ports'. start.grc, reference.grc and variants/*.grc keep only id 'sig_source_msg_ports', title, generate_options and output_language: seedtools.headless_seed keeps only these four, and build.py sets options.parameters to a fixed dict. task.json license says 'GPL-3.0-or-later (derived from ...)' but names no copyright holder and gives no modification date. Eval plan §14 says 'Released items respect their source licences', and GPL-3.0 §4/§5 cover keeping notices and marking modifications. The cause is in the seed tool, so every seed-derived item is affected.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep options.author and options.copyright in the .grc files, or add a source.copyright / attribution field to task.json, for example 'Copyright 2020 Free Software Foundation; author Marcus Müller; modified for GRC-Bench, Oct 2026'. Record the id change and the stripped options in the perturbation or conversion record. The team should decide this once for all seed-derived items.

findings.claim: This item is L1 but built from a converted GNU Radio example. The approved plan's Phase 3 says L1 tasks come from the deterministic composer and L2 tasks from converted examples.
findings.evidence: In C:\Users\Lenovo\.claude\plans\take-a-look-at-cozy-crescent.md, Phase 3 says: 'Both L1 (from the deterministic composer of ≤ 5-block single-rate chains) and L2 (from converted examples)'. This task is level L1 with source.kind 'gnuradio_example'. It does meet the numeric L1 rule (5 functional blocks: Signal Source, Message Strobe, Message Strobe Random-Delay, Throttle2, File Sink). The slot brief assigned this seed, and splits/flowgraph_seed_split.json estimates its level as L1.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the team confirm that seed-derived L1 items are allowed, or record this as a deviation in the review notes. The level label itself does not need to change.

findings.claim: If an answer drops showports: 'True', GRC hides the cmd port and leaves the message connection out of the generated code without any error. The answer passes V1-V5 and fails only at V6, so the failure is counted as a behaviour error when it is really structural.
findings.evidence: Probe: the reference without showports passes V1-V5 and fails V6 (f2p 1500 Hz / 0.8). The generated Python has no msg_connect from blocks_message_strobe_random_0 to analog_sig_source_x_0. analog_sig_source_x.block.yml has 'hide: ${ not showports }' on the cmd input and default 'False'. The fail verdict is right, and the system prompt only lets models leave out parameters that are at their defaults. But V2's dangling-connection lint does not catch this case, so the ladder funnel will put such answers at V6.
findings.suggested_fix: This is outside the task directory. In _worker._v2, flag connections whose port is hidden or dropped by codegen, or add a note in the task that this failure lands at V6. No change to the task's files is needed.
